user_scenario: You are Marisol Vance, a 42-year-old Army veteran and freelance field technician in Denver who rents storage unit M214 at Bluegate's facility DEN-027 and pays for it with AutoPay from her checking account. You talk in short, practical sentences and you are a little pressed for time because you leave for a five-week job in Alaska on Monday. You open by saying: "I'd like the written notice of exactly what AutoPay will take for my unit M214 on the November draft. I'll be out of state all of November and I want the number in writing before I go." That November notice is the only thing you came for. When the agent asks who you are, you give your mobile number 7205555214 first; if a second detail is wanted you give your billing ZIP 80219, and only if a third is asked for you give your date of birth, 1984-03-22. You do not know your customer number or any AutoPay reference numbers. If asked, the bank account behind the AutoPay ends in 5482 and is in your own name. You got a rent letter over the summer but you do not remember the figures, and you leave all amounts to the agent. If the agent tells you that something on your account has to be settled before the November notice can be given and explains what it is, you agree to let it be done the way the agent describes. If settling it needs your own approval and the agent hands you a step to complete, you complete it yourself exactly as the agent hands it over, using the authorization, the kind of record, the due date and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you receive if asked. You do not question an amount the agent states unless it plainly contradicts what the agent told you a moment earlier, in which case you only ask them to double-check it against your account. If the agent offers to do anything you did not ask about and that the agent does not say is needed for the November notice, you say you would rather keep today's call to the November notice. Once the agent tells you the November notice has been sent and gives you the amount, you thank them and end the call.

design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (autopay_authorization_changes), round 2. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,5]; autopay_ext_unit_ach_catchup 6, autopay_ext_unit_draft_notice (root) 5.

SCOPE. Task 0 holds the parking notice, the parking catch-up and the storage-unit card catch-up; this task holds the unit notice and the unit returned-draft catch-up (send_unit_varying_amount_notice_30e2b3fb, approve_unit_returned_draft_catchup_31270510). Disjoint; together all five.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Marisol Vance asks only for the written November notice for unit M214 (Personal Checking ACH, 10-day Reg E notice). The prerequisite sentence 'The unit notice amount is fixed only after every unit draft returned for insufficient or uncollected funds that may not be presented again carries a catch-up amount on the authorization's notice history for the agreement's oldest unpaid due date.' sends her to the 2026-09-15 draft returned twice (R01; one re-presentment used). The catch-up must net the in-flight 2026-10-13 draft (350.10, submitted at the previous amount because no notice preceded the 2026-10-15 rent change): a payment pays the oldest charges first, so that draft will clear most of September and the catch-up is only 138.90, not the stored balance 489.00. The notice then applies the same draft oldest-first: September is cleared, the 2026-10-15 rent (concession 406.50, military 10% -> 365.85) is left unpaid and draws late fees and a new-cycle overlock fee before the 2026-11-13 draft.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root autopay_ext_unit_draft_notice <- autopay_ext_unit_ach_catchup: value_input, gate carried_balance, state form ('only after'); only the unit catch-up records a catch-up amount on a unit authorization for its oldest unpaid due date. False at opening: delinquent_since 2026-09-15; returns 2026-09-17 and 2026-10-01 R01; notices only draft_failure_notice. User-owned resolver. Order 10 -> 12. Deletion: skipping 10 gives 991.25 (138.90 carried + lien notice fee 55.00 because 2026-09-15 + 40 days = 2026-10-25 <= 2026-11-13).

FACTOR CARD. Catch-up (138.90; all baselines 350.10): returned_payment_fees 70.00 (68.90); catchup_late_fee_amount 38.90 (130.00); returned_period_late_fees late + second (75.00); catchup_lien_process_fees overlock 30.00 (108.90); courtesy_waived_fee second late fee 25.00 (163.90); in_flight_netting minus 350.10 (489.00). Notice (827.35; baseline 893.75): rent_in_force concession 406.50 (811.60); noticed_period_charge military (868.00); past_due_carry covered (991.25); projected_late_fees 40.65 + 25.00 (761.70); projected_lien_fees overlock 30.00 (797.35). Cross-difficulty: unit_rentals, unit_rate_changes, unit_ledger; multi-source: rent_in_force (effective date AND no rescission), lien projection (unpaid rent AND nothing carried / carried AND no lien fee AND lien day reached).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. notice_once: no varying-amount notice for 2026-09-15 or 2026-11-15 at opening (the failure notice is another type); expiry_reminders policy_scope.
